Surviving the Storm

By: Nickolaus Bauer | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
South African living in Spain, shares her harrowing tale of survival during Valencia's catastrophic floods that claimed over 200 lives

Press Release:


Valencian Floods | SA survivor

In late October, South African Lindie Jackson was enjoying another casual day in her new home city, Valencia in Spain, when torrential rains and flooding hit the coastal city. It would become the deadliest flood in modern Spanish history, killing more than 220 people. Within minutes of receiving the flood alert warning, the streets had already been submerged in fast-flowing muddy water. In every street, cars piled on top of each other, pavements were completely ripped up and debris was everywhere. For people like Lindie, the unfolding disaster was a terrifying experience. Lindie shares those harrowing details with Carte Blanche, revealing the devastating role of climate change and governance failures as extreme weather conditions continue to batter cities around the world.

Producer & Presenter: Nickolaus Bauer



Script:


SCENE 1 - INTRO - 0:00 - 0:46
VO:
DISASTER
UPS: Natsound Winds blowing
Visuals:
● Cars being swept away.
● Bonaire mall flooded.
VO:
DESTRUCTION
Visuals:
Cars being swept away. Bonaire mall flooded.
UPS:
“A dios mio! Es una puta locura!” (Oh my god! This is insane!)
VO:
ANGER
VISUALS:
● Angry crowd rioting.
● King Felipe being pelted with mud.
● Desperate woman screaming.
UPS:
“CUANTO DIGAS! CUANTO DIGAS! HIJO DE PUTA!” (What are you going to say!? You bastards!)

Opening PTC
VISUALS:
● PTC
● 2016 flood in Alexandra
PTC:
"This moment takes me back to November 2016 in Alexandra, Johannesburg. 8 years later… That memory is still fresh.Now I leave Madrid and head to Valencia to uncover another tale of loss and survival.
SCENE 2 -TRAVEL TO VALENCIA 0:46 - 1:00
VISUALS:
● SIGNS TO VALENCIA
BAUER DRIVING
VO:

And to meet a South African family who experienced disaster first-hand.
As weather patterns change and intensify due to climate change, impacting every part of the globe… [pause for upsounds from archive]

SCENE 3 -SCENE SETTER 1:00 - 1:31
VISUALS:
● Force of the floods
● Torrential rain
● Destruction of the floods
● GFX & map of Flood area

VO: … the coastal city of Valencia in Spain became the latest victim. A vicious storm named Dana swept over it late last month. A year’s worth of rainfall fell in just 8 hours – more than 300 litres per square meter. Vast parts of the inland coast were submerged, over 200 people died and many more remain missing.

SCENE 4 -LINK PTC 1:31 - 1:51
VISUALS:
● Outside van putting on boots
● Link PTC

LINK PTC VO:
“I’ve covered a lot of disasters as a journalist. But in 15 years of reporting I’ve never witnessed something of this magnitude. This is really something else.”
SCENE 5 -CAR GRAVEYARD SOUTH OF VALENCIA CITY CENTRE 1:51 - 2:36
VISUALS:
● Car graveyard

LINK PTC:
“The power of the flood washed away walls and pieces of entire buildings AND bounced cars around like stones. This vehicle graveyard of vehicles in the south of Valencia’s city centre is a chilling reminder of just how brutal the storm was. Over 3 weeks since the disaster struck they remain after being stacked here by authorities as part of clean up and rescue operations. A grotesque monument if you will to the sheer force of Mother Nature.”

SCENE 6 -DISASTER AFTERMATH 2:36 -3:02
VISUALS:

Army involved in clean up operations
● Interview Byte
VO:
The Spanish army was deployed as part of the recovery. Things won’t be back to normal any time soon. Those affected remain shell shocked - like Valencian resident Ampanro Ruiz.

INTERVIEW BYTE: Ampanro Ruiz, Valencian resident (TRANSLATED) (15 seconds)
CHYRON STRAP - AMPANRO RUIZ - VALENCIAN RESIDENT
“The government arrived but they should have arrived far earlier. We suffered here alone for over a week without help from anyone.”

SCENE 7 - EXPERTS 3:02 - 3:33
VISUALS:
● University of Valencia exterior
● Academics working
VO:
The DANA weather system that delivered these monster storms is a natural phenomenon that Valencia expects every year. But not to this extent.

VO
While climate change played a huge role in the severity of the storm, Dr Ivan Portugues of the University of Valencia argues that many factors were at play.

Dr Ivan Portugues, University of Valencia
CHYRON STRAP - DR IVAN PORTUGUES, UNIVERSITY OF VALENCIA
“One of them is urbanism. So the way we constructed the houses , which are actually settled within a flooded area with very dangerous streams all around.”

SCENE 8 - JACKSON FAMILY INTERVIEW 3:33 - 5:25
VISUALS:
● Flood destruction
● Jacksons at home with their children
VO:
Hundreds of thousands were affected. Among the survivors are South African couple Lindie and Ryan Jackson.

INTERVIEW BYTE: Lindie Jackson, South African in Valencia 17 seconds
CHYRON STRAP - LINDIE JACKSON, SOUTH AFRICAN IN VALENCIA
“Luckily our house is up on the hill, but the water came up right to here. And it was pitch black, everything there was covered. As you can see it tore down the walls. It came up to his balcony.”

VISUALS:
BONAIRE SHOPPING MALL

VO:
That morning Lindie and Ryan kept their kids at home as family were visiting from South Africa. She then made a shopping trip to the local mall with her mother-in-law - some twenty minutes away - when the rain began pelting down.

INTERVIEW BYTE:
Lindie Jackson, South African in Valencia 18 seconds
“There was no civil alerts - no other warnings. It was more internally driven by people sending videos and that’s when we started driving back home with heavy traffic and we had to do a detour because the bridge here was completely under water..

VISUALS:

● Cell phone footage from Lindie’s phone

VO:
Just over a kilometer from home Lindie got stranded as flash floods ripped through her neighborhood

INTERVIEW BYTE:
Nickolaus Bauer
“What went through your mind when the car got stuck?”
Lindie Jackson, South African in Valencia (33 seconds)

“That I wasn’t going to go home. “I was like - this is not how I want to go. You know - I need one last moment at least. So I was like: ‘No! I am going home and I’m putting all my kids in my bed.”

Nickolaus Bauer
“You decided you had to get home, come hell or high water?”

Lindie Jackson, South African in Valencia
“As I put my leg in, my whole foot went in, it was way too deep and it pulled me. Then I knew we couldn’t cross at this point. The road was completely gone. For water to tear a tar road apart - its crazy.”

VISUALS
● Destroyed roads
● Stranded vehicle

VO:
As Lindie sat tight, Ryan left home to rescue her. But he didn’t make it further than a few hundred meters before he had to abandon his car and swim to safety.

Ryan Jackson, South African in Valencia (32 seconds)
CHYRON STRAP - RYAN JACKSON, SOUTH AFRICAN IN VALENCIA
“I got out of my car and I was in water literally under my chest. No matter how many times I walk you through it, it doesn’t explain how intense it was.”

SCENE 9 - FORMER GOVERNMENT OFFICIAL 5:25 - 6:04
VISUALS:



● Celsa Monros on her phone
● Celsa talking to Nickolaus

VO:
Celsa Monros was the director-general of climate change planning in the Valencian government for 3 years before the role was scrapped under a new administration.

Interview byte - Celsa Monros, Former Valencian DG: Climate change planning
CHYRON STRAP - CELSA MONROS, FORMER VALENCIAN DG CLIMATE CHANGE PLANNING

“We have a lot of forecast services. A lot of protocols. But those protocols were not activated. Nobody took decisions previous or even during the event until it was too late.”

Nickolaus Bauer

“So basically what you’re telling me is that this Valencian government doesn’t only not believe in climate change but it ignored the warnings from its own system?”

Interview byte - Celsa Monros, Former Valencian DG: Climate change planning

“Yes that’s correct.”


VISUALS:

● Lindie, Ryan and the kids
● Destroyed Bonaire Mall
● Lindie walking surveying damage

VO:
Lindie waited out the deluge and eventually waded home to safety, where Ryan and the kids were waiting. It was a matter of twenty minutes that saved her life. The mall was one of the first buildings to be completely submerged.

SCENE 10 - RETURN TO THE MALL 6:04 - 6:38
Lindie Jackson, South African in Valencia 20 seconds
“I spoke to a friend - and she’s like: ‘The angels were watching you!’ - But we keep saying: ‘Where was everyone else’s angels?’ It's unreal. We were just super lucky in so many ways. How our house was positioned, not sending the kids to school that day, leaving the mall at that point. I thank god everyday.”


SCENE 11 - CIVIL UNREST 6:38 - 7:28

VISUALS:

● Riot as King Felipe is chased away

VO:
In the days following the disaster the people of Valencia revolted. Throwing mud at Spanish King Felipe when he visited affected areas. Furious at what they believed was an incompetent and slow response from the communal Valencian and national government.

Nickolaus Bauer
“Do you think there would have been this many deaths if they had taken the warnings seriously?”

Interview byte - Celsa Monros, Former Valencian DG: Climate change planning

“I don’t think so. For sure the highways and the houses would have been flooded. But all the amount of people that were out of their houses those people should not have even gone to work according to the red alert the meteorological system was issuing at 8am,”

Nickolaus

“So are we beginning to see the worst of climate change?”

Interview byte - Celsa Monros, Former Valencian DG: Climate change planning

“No. This is the beginning.

SCENE 11 - JACKSON FAMILY AT HOME 7:28 - 8:08
VISUALS:

● Jacksons at home as a family

VO:
The Jacksons are grateful they survived. But are wary of them or their children becoming eventual victims of a rapidly changing climate in a world where governments fail to plan for disasters like this.

Ryan Jackson

“I think that always just holds on the heart of if it ever happens again. We beat it unlike so many. We were this close to coming short.”

Ryan Jackson “I think that always just holds on the heart of if it ever happens again. We beat it unlike so many. We were this close to coming short.”

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): South African living in Spain, shares her harrowing tale of survival during Valencia's catastrophic floods that claimed over 200 lives
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Exclusive with Lindie Jackson a South African survivor of the floods
metadata.Summary: Valencia’s devastating floods claimed over 200 lives and led to a political blame game as the inability to deal with climate disasters even in developed nations is laid bare. Lindie Jackson's story highlights the role of climate change and governance failures in amplifying the impacts of extreme weather,
